units.text: INT. HUSBAND - CONTINUOUS
The candles in the drawing-room are lit, madam, as you directed.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: Thank you.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Rises hastily and slips the letter under a large silver-cased blotting-book that is lying on the table .
I trust the shades will be to your liking, madam. They are the most becoming we have. They are the same as his lordship uses himself when he is dressing for dinner.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: With a smile .
Then I am sure they will be perfectly right.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Gravely .
Thank you, madam.
units.name: PHIPPS

units.text: MRS. CHEVELEY goes into the drawing-room .
PHIPPS closes the door and retires .
The door is then slowly opened , and MRS. CHEVELEY comes out and creeps stealthily towards the writing-table .
Suddenly voices are heard from the smoking-room .
MRS. CHEVELEY grows pale , and stops .
The voices grow louder , and she goes back into the drawing-room , biting her lip .
Enter LORD GORING and LORD CAVERSHAM.
Expostulating .
My dear father, if I am to get married, surely you will allow me to choose the time, place, and person? Particularly the person.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Testily .

That is a matter for me, sir. You would probably make a very poor choice. It is I who should be consulted, not you. There is property at stake. It is not a matter for affection. Affection comes later on in married life.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Yes. In married life affection comes when people thoroughly dislike each other, father, doesn’t it?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Puts on LORD CAVERSHAM’S cloak for him .
Certainly, sir. I mean certainly not, sir. You are talking very foolishly to-night. What I say is that marriage is a matter for common sense.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: But women who have common sense are so curiously plain, father, aren’t they? Of course I only speak from hearsay.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: No woman, plain or pretty, has any common sense at all, sir. Common sense is the privilege of our sex.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Quite so. And we men are so self-sacrificing that we never use it, do we, father?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: I use it, sir. I use nothing else.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: So my mother tells me.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: It is the secret of your mother’s happiness. You are very heartless, sir, very heartless.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: I hope not, father.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Goes out for a moment .
Then returns , looking rather put out , with SIR ROBERT CHILTERN.
My dear Arthur, what a piece of good luck meeting you on the doorstep! Your servant had just told me you were not at home. How extraordinary!
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: The fact is, I am horribly busy to-night, Robert, and I gave orders I was not at home to any one. Even my father had a comparatively cold reception. He complained of a draught the whole time.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Ah! you must be at home to me, Arthur. You are my best friend. Perhaps by to-morrow you will be my only friend. My wife has discovered everything.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Ah! I guessed as much!
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Looking at him .
Really! How?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: After some hesitation .
Oh, merely by something in the expression of your face as you came in. Who told her?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Mrs. Cheveley herself. And the woman I love knows that I began my career with an act of low dishonesty, that I built up my life upon sands of shame—that I sold, like a common huckster, the secret that had been intrusted to me as a man of honour. I thank heaven poor Lord Radley died without knowing that I betrayed him. I would to God I had died before I had been so horribly tempted, or had fallen so low.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Burying his face in his hands .
After a pause .
You have heard nothing from Vienna yet, in answer to your wire?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Looking up .
Yes; I got a telegram from the first secretary at eight o’clock to-night.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Well?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Nothing is absolutely known against her. On the contrary, she occupies a rather high position in society. It is a sort of open secret that Baron Arnheim left her the greater portion of his immense fortune. Beyond that I can learn nothing.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: She doesn’t turn out to be a spy, then?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Oh! spies are of no use nowadays. Their profession is over. The newspapers do their work instead.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: And thunderingly well they do it.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Arthur, I am parched with thirst. May I ring for something? Some hock and seltzer?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN
